text:
alex: Heads-up — after flipping the microkernel-small selector in canary pool-4, host ingress CPU climbed ~8% and grpc smallwrite tail worsened. Anyone looking?

mira: Yep. I replayed a 3k request slice and saw p50 40ms->43ms, p99 260ms->340ms. Flame shows preparse::stitch and serializer::emit_small dominating.

jon: The selector now prefers microkernel-small for seq<=20 to improve batching. That kernel skips the vectorized utf8 scan and does a per-token assemble which can cause extra fragmentation.

alex: Perf sample from a canary box: token_assembler::emit 18.2% | net::writev 12.4% | http2::frame_split 9.0% | kvstore::get 5.1%

perf-watcher: replay summary: 3k reqs baseline p50=40ms p99=260ms; new selector p50=43ms p99=340ms. avg writev/request +20%. KV hit-rate stable.

mira: Trace indicates an extra memcpy per fragment when assembler runs on microkernel-small. On our workload that hits ~30% of requests, hence the syscall tail.

jon: Two immediate options: revert selector on canary, or change the batching hint to prefer coalesce_size=64 for pool-4. I prefer revert first to stop noisy signals.

alex: Agreed — revert on canary. Also add instrumentation: request.metrics.writev_count and request.metrics.memcpy_bytes so we can correlate.

devops-bot: pool-4 rollback initiated by alex at 2026-03-24T01:12:11Z  status: in_progress.

mira: I'll kick a replay A/B as soon as rollback completes. Plan: collector pprof CPU snapshots + lightweight strace to count write syscalls during 2m window.

jon: In parallel I'll draft a hybrid selector: prefer microkernel-small only if fragment_count==0 AND avg_seq_len>=16. That should keep vectorized path for likely-fragment scenarios.

alex: Also consider a kvcache-prefetch hint when selector picks microkernel-small so we can reduce round trips for header-keys we see frequently. That might cut writev ops a bit. Keep it gated.

ci-bot: CI job queued: chooser/hybrid + unit tests (fragment fuzz) -> job #4827.

perf-watcher: Revert completed at 2026-03-24T01:15:02Z  pool-4 back to selector:v4.8. Baseline metrics restored in 1m window.

mira: A/B plan: run replay with tags selector:new, selector:hybrid; collect pprof every 30s for 5m steady windows, record writev_count and memcpy_bytes. Will upload artifacts to s3 when done.

jon: I'll open PR "selector: hybrid microkernel gating + fragment fuzz tests" with bench scripts and perf numbers.

alex: Good. If hybrid keeps host CPU within 2% of baseline and reduces writev_count to near baseline, we can ship with kvcache-prefetch behind a flag.

mira: Uploading short results now: s3://perf/2854321987/ab_summary.csv. Initial look: hybrid p50 ~ baseline +1.2%, writev_count -12% vs new selector, memcpy_bytes down ~30% vs new selector.

jon: Nice. We'll run a longer 4h canary with hybrid and prefetch OFF, then optionally enable prefetch to measure marginal gains.

alex: Also add SLO alert to watch grpc smallwrite tail on the ingress service during rollout.

ci-bot: Unit tests for fragment fuzz added to PR #4890. Bench job attached.

perf-watcher: 4h canary scheduled. Will post consolidated numbers on completion.

mira: Thanks — closing this thread for now, will reopen if any regressions after hybrid lands.
